# The fixture corpus for the differential artifact format

**These bytes were produced by neither the decoder that reads them nor the
encoder that sits beside it.** They were built field by field from the format
specification by a generator that implements crc32c itself and links no part of
this project.

## Why that matters

Every other test in `test/differential_artifact_test.cc` assembles its image
with a helper that computes the trailer using the engine's own `wal::Crc32c`.
Those tests agree with the engine by construction: a shared misreading of field
order, or of what the checksum covers, is invisible to all of them.

These files are the only images the decoder is checked against that it did not
help produce, so they are the only ones that can disagree with it.

> A fixture generated by the production encoder would test that that decoder
> agrees with that encoder — the question a corpus exists to *not* assume.

## THIS CORPUS IS FROZEN

The generator lived in the parent project and did not come across with the
extraction. A second decoder read the same files there; it did not come across
either.

What is in this directory is all there will ever be here:

- a fixture **cannot be regenerated** if it is corrupted or deleted;
- a fixture **cannot be added** for a new refusal rule;
- the expected values in the tests were written from the document, so they
  **cannot be re-derived** from anything in this repository.

**Do not write a replacement with the test file's `Assemble` helper.** An image
built by the code under test proves nothing about the document, and a fixture
that looks like the others while being circular is worse than an absent one.

A format rule added after the split is therefore covered only by the circular
tests. That is a fact to know, not a gap this directory can close.

## What each file is

`legal-*` must be accepted. `refuse-*` must be refused; the specific refusal
that fires is not asserted when a file breaks more than one rule, only that it
is not accepted.
